'''John Wickham Steeds''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS|FInstP}}<ref name="FRS" /> (born 9 February 1940) is a British physicist and [[materials science|materials scientist]]. He is an Emeritus Professor of Physics at the [[University of Bristol]].<ref name="FRS" /><ref name="BristolStaffPage">{{cite web | title=Professor John Steeds - Physics | website=www.bristol.ac.uk | date=2017-02-20 | url=http://www.bristol.ac.uk/physics/people/john-w-steeds/overview.html | access-date=2017-07-13 | archive-date=2017-08-06 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170806053619/http://www.bristol.ac.uk/physics/people/john-w-steeds/overview.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Research ==
Steeds is best known for his investigations of the [[microstructure]] of materials using [[electron microscopy]] and [[Convergent beam electron diffraction|convergent-beam electron diffraction]]. Early in his career, he produced seminal work on [[dislocation]] arrangements in deformed [[copper]] crystals, which is a basis for the more recent theories of [[work hardening]]. His monograph on anisotropic [[elasticity (physics)|elasticity]] theory of dislocations is a standard reference. He has led a sophisticated research effort to make, from image plane diffraction analysis ("real-space [[crystallography]]") and convergent-beam diffraction, a complete system for crystallographic structure determination in the electron microscope. He is recognised as a world expert in this technique.<ref name="HolweckEDPSciences" /><ref name="FRS" />

Significant applications include [[Precipitation hardening|precipitate]] structure in [[steels]], new phases in the contact regions of [[integrated circuit]]s and the correction of important errors in the structure of [[transition metal dichalcogenides]]. With the first observation of [[soliton]]s (discommensurations) in the stripe and triply [[Superstructure (condensed matter)#Incommensurate cases|incommensurate]] states of these layer compounds, he has produced dynamic images of the basic [[phase transition|phase-transition]] mechanisms.<ref name="HolweckEDPSciences" /><ref name="FRS" />

== Awards and honours ==
Steeds was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1988|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1988]].<ref name="FRS">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/john-steeds-12341|title=John Steeds|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|access-date=2017-07-13|archive-date=2015-11-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151123164302/https://royalsociety.org/people/john-steeds-12341/|url-status=dead}} One or more of the preceding sentences may incorporate text from the royalsociety.org website where "all text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License" ([https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies], Intellectual property rights).</ref><ref name="frsCitation">{{cite web|url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqPos=0&dsqSearch=%28RefNo%3D%27EC%2F1988%2F37%27%29|title=EC/1988/37: Steeds, John Wickham|publisher=[[The Royal Society]]|accessdate=13 July 2017}}{{Dead link|date=November 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> In 1996, he received the [[Fernand Holweck Medal and Prize|Holweck Medal]], awarded jointly by the [[Institute of Physics]] and [[Société Française de Physique]].<ref name="HolweckEDPSciences" /><ref name="Holweck">{{cite web | last=Physics | first=Institute of | title=Holweck medal recipients | website=Institute of Physics - For physics • For physicists • For all | url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/bilateral/holweck/medallists/page_38481.html | access-date=2017-07-13}}</ref>
